title: Overseas university graduates in Singapore's fresh graduate employment data
asked: Whether Singaporeans who graduated from overseas universities were included in the September 2025 fresh graduate employment figures, how many of those employed were underemployed, and how recent labour market conditions have affected their outcomes.
response: The September 2025 figures covered graduates of local autonomous universities and did not include Singaporeans who graduated from overseas universities. Using time-related underemployment, the rate for residents aged 25 to 29 who graduated from overseas universities was 0.8% in 2025, against 0.7% for local autonomous university graduates, with around nine in 10 of both groups employed. MOM tracks employment outcomes across institution types through the Labour Force Survey, and support is available through Education and Career Guidance in the IHLs and career matching and coaching by WSG and e2i.

key_points.point: The September 2025 fresh graduate employment figures covered local autonomous university graduates only, not Singaporeans who graduated overseas.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: covered graduates from the local autonomous universities and did not include Singaporeans who graduated from overseas universities

key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: the underemployment rate among residents aged 25 to 29 who graduated from overseas universities was 0.8% in 2025

key_points.point: That 0.8% was about 0.1 percentage points above the 0.7% for local autonomous university graduates.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: slightly above the 0.7% recorded for graduates from local autonomous universities

key_points.point: Around nine in 10 graduates aged 25 to 29 from both local autonomous universities and overseas universities were employed.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng

key_points.point: MOM tracks and monitors employment outcomes across institution types, including overseas universities and local private educational institutions, through the Labour Force Survey.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: MOM tracks as well as monitors the employment outcomes of graduates across various types of institutions

key_points.point: In 2025, employment rates for local autonomous university and overseas university graduates were both above 90%, with a differential of just over 1%.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng

key_points.point: Students and fresh graduates, including those from overseas universities, can use career matching and coaching services from WSG and NTUC's e2i.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: may also make use of the career matching and coaching services offered by Workforce Singapore (WSG) and the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute (e2i)

key_points.point: Total employment growth for 2025 was about 57,300, compared with about 44,500 in 2024.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: the total employment growth, which is about 57,300, was stronger than a year ago, in 2024, which was about 44,500

key_points.point: The share of firms expecting to hire in the next three months edged down from 44% in September 2025 to 43% in December 2025.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
key_points.quote: from 44% in September 2025, to 43% in December 2025

key_points.point: The share of firms expecting to raise wages rose from 19% to about 26% over the same period.
key_points.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
